_validation_note: BROADENED 45-DAY WINDOW APPLIED (April 13 – May 28, 2026) per fallback protocol after 30-day window (April 28 – May 28) returned zero Gate 3 survivors. All five candidates evaluated across both windows failed the seven-point gate. (A) Anna Brawley (Assembly Chair, MOA) — data center ordinance AO 2026-27 passed March 27, outside even the 45-day window (Gate 2 fail on ordinance); chair election (April 28) is procedural with no documentable concrete AI consequence (Gate 3 fail); JBER non-stance (May 5) is not a decision and concerns a matter outside the Assembly's jurisdiction with no outcome-changing effect (Gate 3 fail). (B) Nathan Engel (Alaska Airlines VP Maintenance Operations, Tailsight deployment, April 16) — Gates 1, 2, 5 pass; Gate 3 fails: no Anchorage-bowl tie established, Alaska Airlines and Engel are Seattle-based, no Anchorage-specific sector/dollar/workforce/policy consequence reducible to the required formula; Gate 4 fails: all sources confirmed as press-release reprints with no independently reported coverage confirmed on any live fetch. (C) Billy Wailand (GCI SVP Corporate Development, Quintillion acquisition, April 22) — Gates 1, 2, 5 pass; Gate 3 fails: primary source and ADN article explicitly silent on AI workloads, data center compute, and AI-enabling infrastructure; chain-of-inference reasoning (fiber enables AI) does not satisfy Gate 3. (D) Sioux-Z Marshall (MOA IT Director) — no in-window AI decision found on any fetched source (Gate 2 fail). (E) Patrick Tomco (UAA ASET Lab) — no grants or decisions dated within the 45-day window on any fetched source (Gate 2 fail). The Anchorage AI decision pool is small; primary-source decisions with named individual decision-owners and independently corroborated concrete AI consequences are lower-frequency than general news cycles. A no-target cycle is the correct calibration.
